subject: Long-history summarization eval — recap, model suggestions, and pilot next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya@healthlytics.com>, Tom Baxter <tbaxter@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Long-history summarization eval — recap, model suggestions, and pilot next steps

Thanks again for the demo today — good conversation. Quick recap and a concrete plan so we have alignment next steps.

Summary of need
- Problem: HealthLytics ingests multi-year visit histories (free text + structured notes) and needs condensed, clinically-faithful visit summaries and an event timeline. Typical records reach 20k–40k tokens; you see truncation and missing early-history events today.
- Success metric: summarized notes preserve top-3 clinical events (sensitivity) and timeline fidelity (>90% of events ordered correctly) while keeping token cost reasonable for production.

Key observations from today's call
- Most loss happens around repeat medication changes and early admission notes — truncation removes antecedent context that changes interpretation.
- You prefer deterministic summaries for clinician review (concise but complete) rather than free-form long narratives.

Initial model-fit recommendations (shortlist for eval)
1) rw-extended-30b-64k (recommended): good tradeoff for long KV cache + attention optimizations; expect best fidelity at 32–64k windows.
2) rw-quant-13b-32k (cost-efficient): quantized path; good for throughput tests and catch/regression checks.
3) rw-instruct-7b-16k (baseline): fast, low-cost option for ablation; expect some fidelity drops on deep histories.

Benchmark plan and artifacts attached
- Attached prompt set (healthlytics_long_history_promptset_v1.csv) with 120 paired cases (full history + expected summary + event-extraction labels).
- Attached preliminary benchmarking sheet (hl_bench_32k_results.xlsx) with simulated runs on 5k records (synthetic) and latency/cost numbers.
- Eval dashboard link: https://redwood-internal.eval/hl-7543/dashboard

Quality/regression concerns to monitor
- Truncation bias: important events at the start of history being dropped when token limits force windowing. Propose prefix-preservation and explicit event-prioritization prompts during preprocessing.
- Hallucination on condensed timelines: use extraction QA checks against structured fields (med lists, dates) as a regression gate.

Proposed next steps (concrete)
1) Pilot: 500 de-identified patient histories from HealthLytics (we will run on dedicated test queue) — goal: measure summary fidelity + event extraction precision/recall.
2) Eval run: Redwood will run the three model variants above and return a head-to-head with latency/cost and quality metrics within 7 business days after data receipt.
3) Pricing & SOW: Ben to propose pilot pricing and SOW template; if acceptable, PO and data transfer steps.
4) Deep dive: schedule a 60-minute technical session to review preprocessing and prompt strategies after pilot results.

Can Ben/Neha weigh in on cost estimate and earliest availability to run the eval? Priya/Tom — if that plan looks sensible, we can share the prompt set and a small upload token for the pilot later today.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
